title: Finite cohomology of the uniformizer cone on an integral stalk
statement: Let y be a geometric point of Y, and K an arbitrary integral coefficient complex as in [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Suppose its first derived finite reduction is constructible in the intrinsic sense of [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]. Let C be the termwise integral module stalk, with its canonical constant scalar action. In every integer degree, the homology of the mapping cone of uniformizer multiplication C -> C is a finite set. No completeness, boundedness or finite Tor hypothesis on K is imposed.

from.place: Proof, final paragraph: finite residue reduction and its stalk

proof.text: Choose a flat-term K-flat sheaf resolution P -> K. The completed coefficient projection to the first finite quotient has kernel the uniformizer multiples and is surjective; uniformizer multiplication is injective. These assertions follow objectwise from completedIntegralProjection_divisible, completedIntegralScalar_regular and constantQuotient_surjective, and imply a short exact coefficient sequence.

source.place: Proof, final paragraph: finite residue reduction and its stalk

proof.text: Tensor this short exact coefficient sequence with each flat term of P. Its third term is restriction of the ordinary scalar extension of P, and K-flatness makes this extension a representative of the first derived reduction. Thus the cone of uniformizer multiplication on P represents the restricted derived reduction. The same coefficient diagram shows that its scalar is the specified constant scalar, not an unspecified action.

source.place: Proof, final paragraph: finite residue reduction and its stalk

proof.text: Apply the exact integral stalk. It preserves the cone and identifies its cohomology with the stalk cohomology of the restricted first reduction. Intrinsic constructibility descends through the exact finite-coefficient realization equivalence to a constructible etale sheaf. The canonical comparison of geometric stalks makes each of these cohomology stalks finite.

source.place: Proof, final paragraph: finite residue reduction and its stalk

proof.text: The quasi-isomorphism P -> K commutes with uniformizer multiplication. Its induced morphism between the cones is a quasi-isomorphism by the long exact cohomology sequences. Transport finiteness to the cone built from the specified K.

theorem integralStalk_residue_finite
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra ℚ_[l] E]
    [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E] (y : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ Y)
    (K : CochainComplex (scalarReductionSource.{u, u} l E Y) ℤ)
    (hred : intrinsicFiniteTorsionConstructible l E 1 (by omega) Y
      ((scalarReductionDerivedExtension.{u, u} l E Y 0).obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K))) :
    let R := ULift.{u + 1, u} (Padic.coefficientExtensionIntegers l E)
    let C := ((integralCoefficientModuleStalkFunctor l E y).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj K
    ∀ i : ℤ, Finite ((HomologicalComplex.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u + 1} R) (.up ℤ) i).obj
      (CochainComplex.mappingCone ((ULift.up
        (Padic.coefficientExtensionUniformizer l E)) • 𝟙 C)))
